solution:
\(\cot 50^\circ = \tan(90^\circ - 50^\circ) = \tan 40^\circ\), so L.H.S. \(= \tan 20^\circ\,\tan 40^\circ\,\tan 80^\circ\).

First a general result. With \(t = \tan\theta\),
\(\tan(60^\circ-\theta)\,\tan(60^\circ+\theta) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}-t}{1+\sqrt{3}\,t}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+t}{1-\sqrt{3}\,t} = \dfrac{3-t^{2}}{1-3t^{2}}\),
so \(\tan\theta\,\tan(60^\circ-\theta)\,\tan(60^\circ+\theta) = \dfrac{3t-t^{3}}{1-3t^{2}} = \tan 3\theta\).

Putting \(\theta = 20^\circ\) (so \(60^\circ-\theta = 40^\circ\), \(60^\circ+\theta = 80^\circ\)):
\(\tan 20^\circ\,\tan 40^\circ\,\tan 80^\circ = \tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}\).

\(\therefore \tan 20^\circ\,\tan 80^\circ\,\cot 50^\circ = \sqrt{3} = \) R.H.S.

\(\sin\alpha\,\sin\beta - \cos\alpha\,\cos\beta + 1 = 0\)

\(\therefore -(\cos\alpha\,\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\,\sin\beta) + 1 = 0\), i.e. \(-\cos(\alpha+\beta) + 1 = 0\).

\(\therefore \cos(\alpha+\beta) = 1\), so \(\alpha + \beta = 2n\pi\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\), i.e. \(\beta = 2n\pi - \alpha\).

\(\therefore \tan\beta = \tan(2n\pi - \alpha) = -\tan\alpha\).

\(\therefore \cot\alpha\,\tan\beta = \cot\alpha\,(-\tan\alpha) = -\tan\alpha\,\cot\alpha = -1 = \) R.H.S.

Let \(\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{15}\). The four angles are \(\theta,\ 2\theta,\ 4\theta,\ 8\theta\).

Multiply and divide by \(2\sin\theta\) and use \(2\sin\phi\cos\phi = \sin 2\phi\) repeatedly:
\(\cos\theta\,\cos 2\theta\,\cos 4\theta\,\cos 8\theta = \dfrac{2\sin\theta\cos\theta\cdot\cos 2\theta\cos 4\theta\cos 8\theta}{2\sin\theta} = \dfrac{\sin 16\theta}{16\sin\theta}\).

Here \(16\theta = \dfrac{32\pi}{15} = 2\pi + \dfrac{2\pi}{15}\), so \(\sin 16\theta = \sin\dfrac{2\pi}{15} = \sin\theta\).

\(\therefore \cos\dfrac{2\pi}{15}\,\cos\dfrac{4\pi}{15}\,\cos\dfrac{8\pi}{15}\,\cos\dfrac{16\pi}{15} = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{16\sin\theta} = \dfrac{1}{16} = \) R.H.S.

\(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{8} = \cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right) = -\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\) and \(\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{8} = \cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{8}\right) = -\cos\dfrac{\pi}{8}\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= \left(1+\cos\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right)\left(1-\cos\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right)\left(1+\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right)\left(1-\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right) = \sin^{2}\dfrac{\pi}{8}\,\sin^{2}\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\).

Since \(\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{8} = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{8}\right) = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{8}\),
L.H.S. \(= \left(\sin\dfrac{\pi}{8}\cos\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right)^{2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2}\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{1}{8} = \) R.H.S.

Pair the terms as \((\cos 12^\circ + \cos 132^\circ) + (\cos 84^\circ + \cos 156^\circ)\) and use \(\cos C + \cos D = 2\cos\dfrac{C+D}{2}\cos\dfrac{C-D}{2}\):

\(\cos 12^\circ + \cos 132^\circ = 2\cos 72^\circ\,\cos 60^\circ = 2\cos 72^\circ\times\dfrac{1}{2} = \cos 72^\circ\),
\(\cos 84^\circ + \cos 156^\circ = 2\cos 120^\circ\,\cos 36^\circ = 2\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\cos 36^\circ = -\cos 36^\circ\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= \cos 72^\circ - \cos 36^\circ = \sin 18^\circ - \cos 36^\circ\).

Using \(\sin 18^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}\) and \(\cos 36^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}\),
L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4} - \dfrac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4} = -\dfrac{2}{4}\).

\(\therefore \cos 12^\circ + \cos 84^\circ + \cos 156^\circ + \cos 132^\circ = -\dfrac{1}{2} = \) R.H.S.

Use \(\cos C + \cos D = 2\cos\dfrac{C+D}{2}\cos\dfrac{C-D}{2}\) with \(C = \dfrac{\pi}{4}+x\) and \(D = \dfrac{\pi}{4}-x\).

Here \(\dfrac{C+D}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\) and \(\dfrac{C-D}{2} = x\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= 2\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}\,\cos x = 2\times\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\times\cos x\).

\(\therefore \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}+x\right) + \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-x\right) = \sqrt{2}\,\cos x = \) R.H.S.

Numerator: group the outer terms first.
\((\sin 5x + \sin x) - 2\sin 3x = 2\sin 3x\,\cos 2x - 2\sin 3x = 2\sin 3x(\cos 2x - 1)\).
Since \(\cos 2x - 1 = -2\sin^{2}x\), the numerator \(= -4\sin 3x\,\sin^{2}x\).

Denominator: \(\cos 5x - \cos x = -2\sin 3x\,\sin 2x = -2\sin 3x\,(2\sin x\cos x) = -4\sin 3x\,\sin x\,\cos x\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{-4\sin 3x\,\sin^{2}x}{-4\sin 3x\,\sin x\,\cos x} = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\).

\(\therefore \dfrac{\sin 5x - 2\sin 3x + \sin x}{\cos 5x - \cos x} = \tan x = \) R.H.S.

For any \(A\) and \(B\),
\(\sin^{2}A - \sin^{2}B = \dfrac{1-\cos 2A}{2} - \dfrac{1-\cos 2B}{2} = \dfrac{\cos 2B - \cos 2A}{2} = \dfrac{2\sin(A+B)\sin(A-B)}{2} = \sin(A+B)\,\sin(A-B)\).

Put \(A = 6x\) and \(B = 4x\):
L.H.S. \(= \sin(6x+4x)\,\sin(6x-4x) = \sin 10x\,\sin 2x\).

\(\therefore \sin^{2}6x - \sin^{2}4x = \sin 2x\,\sin 10x = \) R.H.S.

\(\cos^{2}2x - \cos^{2}6x = \dfrac{1+\cos 4x}{2} - \dfrac{1+\cos 12x}{2} = \dfrac{\cos 4x - \cos 12x}{2}\).

Now \(\cos C - \cos D = 2\sin\dfrac{C+D}{2}\sin\dfrac{D-C}{2}\), so with \(C = 4x\), \(D = 12x\),
\(\cos 4x - \cos 12x = 2\sin 8x\,\sin 4x\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{2\sin 8x\,\sin 4x}{2}\).

\(\therefore \cos^{2}2x - \cos^{2}6x = \sin 4x\,\sin 8x = \) R.H.S.

Use \(\sin C + \sin D = 2\sin\dfrac{C+D}{2}\cos\dfrac{C-D}{2}\) and \(\sin C - \sin D = 2\cos\dfrac{C+D}{2}\sin\dfrac{C-D}{2}\):
\(\sin 5x + \sin 3x = 2\sin 4x\,\cos x\) and \(\sin 5x - \sin 3x = 2\cos 4x\,\sin x\).

L.H.S. \(= \cot 4x\,(2\sin 4x\cos x) = \dfrac{\cos 4x}{\sin 4x}\times 2\sin 4x\,\cos x = 2\cos 4x\,\cos x\).

R.H.S. \(= \cot x\,(2\cos 4x\sin x) = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\times 2\cos 4x\,\sin x = 2\cos 4x\,\cos x\).

\(\therefore \cot 4x\,(\sin 5x + \sin 3x) = \cot x\,(\sin 5x - \sin 3x)\), i.e. L.H.S. \(= \) R.H.S.

Numerator: \(\cos 9x - \cos 5x = -2\sin\dfrac{9x+5x}{2}\,\sin\dfrac{9x-5x}{2} = -2\sin 7x\,\sin 2x\).

Denominator: \(\sin 17x - \sin 3x = 2\cos\dfrac{17x+3x}{2}\,\sin\dfrac{17x-3x}{2} = 2\cos 10x\,\sin 7x\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{-2\sin 7x\,\sin 2x}{2\cos 10x\,\sin 7x}\).

\(\therefore \dfrac{\cos 9x - \cos 5x}{\sin 17x - \sin 3x} = -\dfrac{\sin 2x}{\cos 10x} = \) R.H.S.

Given \(\sin 2A = \lambda\sin 2B\), so \(\dfrac{\sin 2A}{\sin 2B} = \lambda\) (with \(\lambda \ne 1\), so that \(\lambda - 1 \ne 0\)).

By componendo and dividendo,
\(\dfrac{\sin 2A + \sin 2B}{\sin 2A - \sin 2B} = \dfrac{\lambda + 1}{\lambda - 1}\).

Now \(\sin 2A + \sin 2B = 2\sin(A+B)\cos(A-B)\) and \(\sin 2A - \sin 2B = 2\cos(A+B)\sin(A-B)\).

\(\therefore \dfrac{\lambda+1}{\lambda-1} = \dfrac{2\sin(A+B)\cos(A-B)}{2\cos(A+B)\sin(A-B)} = \dfrac{\sin(A+B)}{\cos(A+B)}\times\dfrac{\cos(A-B)}{\sin(A-B)} = \dfrac{\tan(A+B)}{\tan(A-B)}\).

\(\therefore \dfrac{\tan (A + B)}{\tan (A - B)} = \dfrac{\lambda + 1}{\lambda - 1} = \) R.H.S.

Start from the R.H.S. and put \(t = \tan A\).

\(\tan(60^\circ+A)\,\tan(60^\circ-A) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}+t}{1-\sqrt{3}\,t}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-t}{1+\sqrt{3}\,t} = \dfrac{3-t^{2}}{1-3t^{2}}\).

Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\cos^{2}A\) gives \(\dfrac{3\cos^{2}A - \sin^{2}A}{\cos^{2}A - 3\sin^{2}A}\).

Using \(\cos^{2}A = \dfrac{1+\cos 2A}{2}\) and \(\sin^{2}A = \dfrac{1-\cos 2A}{2}\):
numerator \(= \dfrac{3+3\cos 2A-1+\cos 2A}{2} = \dfrac{2+4\cos 2A}{2} = 2\cos 2A + 1\),
denominator \(= \dfrac{1+\cos 2A-3+3\cos 2A}{2} = \dfrac{4\cos 2A-2}{2} = 2\cos 2A - 1\).

\(\therefore \dfrac{2\cos 2A + 1}{2\cos 2A - 1} = \tan (60^\circ + A)\,\tan (60^\circ - A)\), i.e. L.H.S. \(= \) R.H.S.

Let \(T = \tan 3A\).

Tripling each of the angles \(A,\ 60^\circ+A,\ 120^\circ+A\) gives \(3A,\ 3A+180^\circ,\ 3A+360^\circ\), and since the period of the tangent is \(180^\circ\), all three have the same tangent \(T\).

So each of \(x = \tan A,\ \tan(60^\circ+A),\ \tan(120^\circ+A)\) satisfies \(T = \dfrac{3x-x^{3}}{1-3x^{2}}\), i.e.
\(T(1-3x^{2}) = 3x - x^{3}\), i.e. \(x^{3} - 3T x^{2} - 3x + T = 0\).

The three tangents are distinct, so they are precisely the three roots of this cubic, and the sum of the roots of \(x^{3} - 3Tx^{2} - 3x + T = 0\) is \(3T\).

\(\therefore \tan A + \tan (60^\circ + A) + \tan (120^\circ + A) = 3T = 3\tan 3A = \) R.H.S.

For any \(\theta\),
\(\cot\dfrac{\theta}{2} - \cot\theta = \dfrac{\cos\frac{\theta}{2}}{\sin\frac{\theta}{2}} - \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} = \dfrac{\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\sin\theta - \cos\theta\sin\frac{\theta}{2}}{\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\,\sin\theta} = \dfrac{\sin\left(\theta - \frac{\theta}{2}\right)}{\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\,\sin\theta} = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta} = \operatorname{cosec}\theta\).

Applying this with \(\theta = 48^\circ,\ 96^\circ,\ 192^\circ,\ 384^\circ\), the sum telescopes:
L.H.S. \(= (\cot 24^\circ - \cot 48^\circ) + (\cot 48^\circ - \cot 96^\circ) + (\cot 96^\circ - \cot 192^\circ) + (\cot 192^\circ - \cot 384^\circ)\)
\(= \cot 24^\circ - \cot 384^\circ\).

Since \(384^\circ = 360^\circ + 24^\circ\), \(\cot 384^\circ = \cot 24^\circ\).

\(\therefore \operatorname{cosec} 48^\circ + \operatorname{cosec} 96^\circ + \operatorname{cosec} 192^\circ + \operatorname{cosec} 384^\circ = \cot 24^\circ - \cot 24^\circ = 0 = \) R.H.S.

For any \(\theta\),
\(\cot\theta - \tan\theta = \dfrac{\cos^{2}\theta - \sin^{2}\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \dfrac{\cos 2\theta}{\frac{1}{2}\sin 2\theta} = 2\cot 2\theta\),
that is, \(2\cot 2\theta + \tan\theta = \cot\theta\).

Now collect the L.H.S. from the right-hand end, using this result three times:
\(8\cot 8A + 4\tan 4A = 4(2\cot 8A + \tan 4A) = 4\cot 4A\),
\(4\cot 4A + 2\tan 2A = 2(2\cot 4A + \tan 2A) = 2\cot 2A\),
\(2\cot 2A + \tan A = \cot A\).

\(\therefore \tan A + 2\tan 2A + 4\tan 4A + 8\cot 8A = \cot A = \) R.H.S.

Given \(A + B + C = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\), so \(A + B = \dfrac{3\pi}{2} - C\).

Hence \(\cos(A+B) = \cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2} - C\right) = -\sin C\), and equally \(\sin C = \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2} - (A+B)\right) = -\cos(A+B)\).

Now \(\cos 2A + \cos 2B = 2\cos(A+B)\cos(A-B) = -2\sin C\,\cos(A-B)\), and \(\cos 2C = 1 - 2\sin^{2}C\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= 1 - 2\sin^{2}C - 2\sin C\cos(A-B) = 1 - 2\sin C\,[\,\sin C + \cos(A-B)\,]\).

Since \(\sin C = -\cos(A+B)\),
\(\sin C + \cos(A-B) = \cos(A-B) - \cos(A+B) = 2\sin A\,\sin B\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= 1 - 2\sin C\,(2\sin A\sin B)\).

\(\therefore \cos 2A + \cos 2B + \cos 2C = 1 - 4\sin A\,\sin B\,\sin C = \) R.H.S.

In \(\Delta ABC\), \(A + B + C = \pi\), so \(\dfrac{B+C}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{A}{2}\) and therefore \(\cos\dfrac{B+C}{2} = \sin\dfrac{A}{2}\).

The given condition \(\sin A - \cos B = \cos C\) means \(\sin A = \cos B + \cos C\), i.e.
\(2\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\cos\dfrac{A}{2} = 2\cos\dfrac{B+C}{2}\,\cos\dfrac{B-C}{2} = 2\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\,\cos\dfrac{B-C}{2}\).

Since \(0 < A < \pi\), \(\sin\dfrac{A}{2} \ne 0\), so it may be cancelled:
\(\cos\dfrac{A}{2} = \cos\dfrac{B-C}{2}\).

Both \(\dfrac{A}{2}\) and \(\dfrac{|B-C|}{2}\) lie in \(\left[0,\ \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\), on which the cosine is one-to-one, so \(A = |B - C|\).

Taking \(A = B - C\) (the case in which \(B\) is the larger of the two) gives \(A + C = B\), so
\(\pi = A + B + C = B + B = 2B\).

\(\therefore \angle B = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
_note: The stated conclusion is INCOMPLETE as printed. Cancelling gives cos(A/2) = cos((B-C)/2), hence A = |B - C|, which splits into TWO cases: A = B - C forces B = pi/2 (the required result), but A = C - B forces C = pi/2. The second branch is genuine, not an artifact: A = 30 deg, B = 60 deg, C = 90 deg satisfies sin A - cos B = 0.5 - 0.5 = 0 = cos C while B = 60 deg is NOT a right angle (verified to 30 significant digits; a grid scan over the whole triangle found no solutions other than these two families). So the correct conclusion is that the triangle is right-angled at B OR at C; the book takes only the branch A = B - C. The proof above follows the book's intended branch. Separately, the stem omits the conditional 'if' before 'sin A - cos B = cos C'.

solution:
Use \(1 + \tan^{2}x = \sec^{2}x\) and \(1 + \cot^{2}x = \operatorname{cosec}^{2}x\):

\(\dfrac{\tan^{3}x}{1+\tan^{2}x} = \dfrac{\tan^{3}x}{\sec^{2}x} = \dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{\cos^{3}x}\times\cos^{2}x = \dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{\cos x}\),
\(\dfrac{\cot^{3}x}{1+\cot^{2}x} = \dfrac{\cot^{3}x}{\operatorname{cosec}^{2}x} = \dfrac{\cos^{3}x}{\sin^{3}x}\times\sin^{2}x = \dfrac{\cos^{3}x}{\sin x}\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{\cos x} + \dfrac{\cos^{3}x}{\sin x} = \dfrac{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}{\sin x\,\cos x}\).

Since \(\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x = (\sin^{2}x+\cos^{2}x)^{2} - 2\sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x = 1 - 2\sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x\),
L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{1 - 2\sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x}{\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{1}{\sin x\cos x} - 2\sin x\cos x\).

\(\therefore \dfrac{\tan^{3}x}{1+\tan^{2}x} + \dfrac{\cot^{3}x}{1+\cot^{2}x} = \sec x\,\operatorname{cosec} x - 2\sin x\,\cos x = \) R.H.S.

First a general result. Using \(\sin(P+Q)\sin(P-Q) = \sin^{2}P - \sin^{2}Q\) with \(P = 60^\circ\), \(Q = \theta\):
\(\sin(60^\circ-\theta)\,\sin(60^\circ+\theta) = \sin^{2}60^\circ - \sin^{2}\theta = \dfrac{3}{4} - \sin^{2}\theta\).

\(\therefore \sin\theta\,\sin(60^\circ-\theta)\,\sin(60^\circ+\theta) = \sin\theta\left(\dfrac{3}{4} - \sin^{2}\theta\right) = \dfrac{3\sin\theta - 4\sin^{3}\theta}{4} = \dfrac{\sin 3\theta}{4}\).

Putting \(\theta = 20^\circ\) (so \(60^\circ-\theta = 40^\circ\), \(60^\circ+\theta = 80^\circ\)):
\(\sin 20^\circ\,\sin 40^\circ\,\sin 80^\circ = \dfrac{\sin 60^\circ}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

\(\therefore \sin 20^\circ\,\sin 40^\circ\,\sin 80^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{8} = \) R.H.S.

Let \(\theta = 18^\circ\). Then \(5\theta = 90^\circ\), so \(2\theta = 90^\circ - 3\theta\) and hence
\(\sin 2\theta = \sin(90^\circ - 3\theta) = \cos 3\theta\).

\(\therefore 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 4\cos^{3}\theta - 3\cos\theta = \cos\theta\,(4\cos^{2}\theta - 3)\).

Since \(\cos 18^\circ \ne 0\), divide by \(\cos\theta\):
\(2\sin\theta = 4\cos^{2}\theta - 3 = 4(1-\sin^{2}\theta) - 3 = 1 - 4\sin^{2}\theta\),
i.e. \(4\sin^{2}\theta + 2\sin\theta - 1 = 0\).

\(\therefore \sin\theta = \dfrac{-2 \pm \sqrt{4 + 16}}{8} = \dfrac{-2 \pm 2\sqrt{5}}{8} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{4}\).

As \(18^\circ\) is acute, \(\sin 18^\circ > 0\), so the root \(\dfrac{-1-\sqrt{5}}{4}\) is rejected.

\(\therefore \sin 18^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{4} = \) R.H.S.

Take \(36^\circ = 2 \times 18^\circ\) and use \(\cos 2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^{2}\theta\):
\(\cos 36^\circ = 1 - 2\sin^{2}18^\circ\).

Now \(\sin 18^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}\) (proved above), so
\(\sin^{2}18^\circ = \dfrac{(\sqrt{5}-1)^{2}}{16} = \dfrac{5 - 2\sqrt{5} + 1}{16} = \dfrac{6 - 2\sqrt{5}}{16}\).

\(\therefore \cos 36^\circ = 1 - 2\times\dfrac{6-2\sqrt{5}}{16} = 1 - \dfrac{6-2\sqrt{5}}{8} = \dfrac{8 - 6 + 2\sqrt{5}}{8} = \dfrac{2 + 2\sqrt{5}}{8}\).

\(\therefore \cos 36^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{5} + 1}{4} = \) R.H.S.

Use \(\sin^{2}36^\circ = 1 - \cos^{2}36^\circ\) with \(\cos 36^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}\) (proved above).

\(\cos^{2}36^\circ = \dfrac{(\sqrt{5}+1)^{2}}{16} = \dfrac{5 + 2\sqrt{5} + 1}{16} = \dfrac{6 + 2\sqrt{5}}{16}\).

\(\therefore \sin^{2}36^\circ = 1 - \dfrac{6+2\sqrt{5}}{16} = \dfrac{16 - 6 - 2\sqrt{5}}{16} = \dfrac{10 - 2\sqrt{5}}{16}\).

As \(36^\circ\) is acute, \(\sin 36^\circ > 0\), so the positive square root is taken.

\(\therefore \sin 36^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{10 - 2\sqrt{5}}}{4} = \) R.H.S.

Here \(\dfrac{\pi^{c}}{8}\) means \(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\) radians, i.e. \(22\dfrac{1}{2}^\circ\). Put \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{8}\), so that \(2\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

From \(\cos 2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^{2}\theta\),
\(\sin^{2}\dfrac{\pi}{8} = \dfrac{1 - \cos\frac{\pi}{4}}{2} = \dfrac{1 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{2-\sqrt{2}}{4}\).

\(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\) lies in the first quadrant, so \(\sin\dfrac{\pi}{8} > 0\) and the positive square root is taken.

\(\therefore \sin\dfrac{\pi}{8} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2-\sqrt{2}}}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{2 - \sqrt{2}} = \) R.H.S.

Let \(t = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{8}\). Since \(2\times\dfrac{\pi}{8} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\), use \(\tan 2\theta = \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1-\tan^{2}\theta}\):

\(\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{2t}{1-t^{2}} = 1\).

\(\therefore 2t = 1 - t^{2}\), i.e. \(t^{2} + 2t - 1 = 0\).

\(\therefore t = \dfrac{-2 \pm \sqrt{4+4}}{2} = \dfrac{-2 \pm 2\sqrt{2}}{2} = -1 \pm \sqrt{2}\).

\(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\) lies in the first quadrant, so \(t > 0\) and the root \(-1-\sqrt{2}\) is rejected.

\(\therefore \tan\dfrac{\pi}{8} = \sqrt{2} - 1 = \) R.H.S.

Use \(\tan\theta\,\tan(60^\circ-\theta)\,\tan(60^\circ+\theta) = \tan 3\theta\) (proved in Q.1) twice.

With \(\theta = 6^\circ\): \(\tan 6^\circ\,\tan 54^\circ\,\tan 66^\circ = \tan 18^\circ\), so \(\tan 6^\circ\,\tan 66^\circ = \dfrac{\tan 18^\circ}{\tan 54^\circ}\).

With \(\theta = 18^\circ\): \(\tan 18^\circ\,\tan 42^\circ\,\tan 78^\circ = \tan 54^\circ\), so \(\tan 42^\circ\,\tan 78^\circ = \dfrac{\tan 54^\circ}{\tan 18^\circ}\).

Multiplying the two results,
L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\tan 18^\circ}{\tan 54^\circ}\times\dfrac{\tan 54^\circ}{\tan 18^\circ}\).

\(\therefore \tan 6^\circ\,\tan 42^\circ\,\tan 66^\circ\,\tan 78^\circ = 1 = \) R.H.S.

Pair the terms as \((\sin 47^\circ - \sin 11^\circ) + (\sin 61^\circ - \sin 25^\circ)\) and use \(\sin C - \sin D = 2\cos\dfrac{C+D}{2}\sin\dfrac{C-D}{2}\):

\(\sin 47^\circ - \sin 11^\circ = 2\cos 29^\circ\,\sin 18^\circ\),
\(\sin 61^\circ - \sin 25^\circ = 2\cos 43^\circ\,\sin 18^\circ\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= 2\sin 18^\circ\,(\cos 29^\circ + \cos 43^\circ) = 2\sin 18^\circ\times 2\cos 36^\circ\cos 7^\circ = 4\sin 18^\circ\cos 36^\circ\cos 7^\circ\).

Now \(4\sin 18^\circ\cos 36^\circ = 4\times\dfrac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4} = \dfrac{5-1}{4} = 1\).

\(\therefore \sin 47^\circ + \sin 61^\circ - \sin 11^\circ - \sin 25^\circ = \cos 7^\circ = \) R.H.S.

L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sin 20^\circ} - \dfrac{1}{\cos 20^\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}\cos 20^\circ - \sin 20^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ\,\cos 20^\circ}\).

Numerator \(= 2\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos 20^\circ - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin 20^\circ\right) = 2(\sin 60^\circ\cos 20^\circ - \cos 60^\circ\sin 20^\circ) = 2\sin(60^\circ - 20^\circ) = 2\sin 40^\circ\).

Denominator \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\,(2\sin 20^\circ\cos 20^\circ) = \dfrac{1}{2}\sin 40^\circ\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{2\sin 40^\circ}{\frac{1}{2}\sin 40^\circ}\).

\(\therefore \sqrt{3}\,\operatorname{cosec} 20^\circ - \sec 20^\circ = 4 = \) R.H.S.

In \(\Delta ABC\), \(A + B + C = \pi\). Given \(\angle C = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\), so \(A + B = \pi - \dfrac{2\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\), and hence \(\cos(A+B) = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

\(\cos^{2}A + \cos^{2}B = \dfrac{1+\cos 2A}{2} + \dfrac{1+\cos 2B}{2} = 1 + \dfrac{\cos 2A + \cos 2B}{2} = 1 + \cos(A+B)\cos(A-B) = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos(A-B)\).

\(\cos A\,\cos B = \dfrac{1}{2}\,[\cos(A-B) + \cos(A+B)] = \dfrac{1}{2}\cos(A-B) + \dfrac{1}{4}\).

\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos(A-B) - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos(A-B) - \dfrac{1}{4} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{4}\).

\(\therefore \cos^{2}A + \cos^{2}B - \cos A\,\cos B = \dfrac{3}{4} = \) R.H.S.
